title: Remove Duplicates, Keep First-Seen Order
statement:
Sorting a vector to group duplicates together is the tempting first idea
for removing them, and it is the wrong tool here: sorting also throws away
the original order, and this exercise needs that order kept. An
`std::unordered_set<int>` gives you O(1) average "have I seen this value
before" without touching the order of anything.

## Your function

```
std::vector<int> DedupePreserveOrder(const std::vector<int>& values);
```

Return `values` with every element after its first occurrence removed, in
the same order the surviving elements appeared in `values`. `values` may
be empty.

## Watch out

- **`unordered_set<int>::insert` tells you whether the value was new, in
  the same call that records it.** It returns a `std::pair<iterator,
  bool>` whose `.second` is `true` exactly when the value was not already
  in the set -- one call answers both "have I seen this" and "remember
  that I have now", rather than needing a separate `.count()` check
  followed by a separate `.insert()`.
- **The output order is the order values first appeared in the input, not
  numeric order and not the `unordered_set`'s own (unspecified) iteration
  order.** Build the result by walking `values` once, appending an element
  only the first time its value is seen -- never by iterating the set
  itself, whose element order the standard does not define at all.
- A value that never repeats still belongs in the result exactly once --
  "first occurrence" includes an element with no duplicates to remove.

generator.source:
"""Random arrays over a small alphabet of values, so repeats are frequent
and the first-seen order is meaningfully tested."""


def generate(rng, count):
    return [_case(rng, i + 1) for i in range(count)]


def _case(rng, index):
    n = rng.randint(0, 20)
    values = [rng.randint(0, 6) for _ in range(n)]
    lines = [str(n)] + [str(v) for v in values]
    return {"name": "%d values from a small pool, repeats likely #%d"
                    % (n, index),
            "stdin": " ".join(lines) + "\n"}

tests.name: every element is the same value
order follows first appearance, not numeric order
tests.description: 3 appears first even though 1 and 2 are smaller -- the result is not sorted.
